question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Acute degron depletion staged across a pulse-chase: Tag FOS/JUN family members with an auxin or dTAG degron and deplete AP-1 either during a transient stimulus or only after it has been withdrawn, then assay whether the stimulus-induced state persists. This separates a role for AP-1 in establishing a state from a requirement for continuous AP-1 activity to maintain it, which is the core claim of a memory mechanism.
2. Heritability of AP-1 activity across cell divisions by live imaging: Build a fluorescent AP-1 (TRE) transcriptional reporter plus an endogenous JUN/FOS protein tag, and track individual cells through several divisions to compute mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations and the autocorrelation half-life of AP-1 activity. Memory predicts correlations that persist well beyond the protein and mRNA turnover timescale and are transmitted through mitosis.
3. Chromatin priming and re-stimulation kinetics at AP-1 motifs: Perform time-resolved ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and footprinting after stimulus withdrawal to identify regions that stay accessible without ongoing signaling, then re-challenge cells and ask whether those primed, AP-1-motif-containing enhancers are the ones that reactivate faster or more strongly. Causality can be tested by CRISPRi or base-editing the AP-1 motifs in the retained peaks.
4. Lineage barcoding to link prior AP-1 state to later cell fate: Barcode cells, sort or record high- versus low-AP-1 cells using a reporter at an early timepoint, and then assay the fate of their barcode-matched descendants (e.g., drug survival, differentiation, invasion) days to weeks later. A memory mechanism predicts that early AP-1 state predicts clonally concordant later outcomes, and that perturbing AP-1 in the interim erases that predictive power.
5. Hysteresis and feedback test with a tunable synthetic AP-1 circuit: Drive AP-1 activity with a dose-tunable inducible FOS/JUN construct and measure the output while ramping the input up and then back down, looking for bistability and hysteresis rather than a single dose-response curve. Pair this with mapping AP-1 binding at its own and its partners' loci to test whether an autoregulatory positive-feedback loop, the simplest molecular basis for such memory, is actually wired in the cell type of interest.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Cis vs. trans memory via twin identical reporters
ideas.description: Integrate two spectrally distinct but sequence-identical AP-1-responsive reporters at different genomic loci in the same cell and track both after a stimulus pulse. Locus-autonomous chromatin memory predicts the two reporters decorrelate and decay independently, while cell-wide protein/feedback memory predicts they remain tightly correlated, separating the two leading mechanistic classes with one measurement.

ideas.title: Clock vs. counter: does the state decay per hour or per division?
ideas.description: Compare decay of the stimulus-induced state in cell-cycle-arrested versus cycling cells (CDK4/6 inhibition, serum starvation, contact inhibition) over matched wall-clock time, and use EdU- or sister-chromatid-resolved readouts to test whether loss occurs specifically at replication. Template-copied chromatin memory should decay per division, whereas protein-level or metabolic memory decays per hour.

ideas.title: Kinetic and dimer-composition signature of the memory state
ideas.description: Apply single-molecule tracking of HaloTagged JUN/FOS in live nuclei together with two-color single-molecule pull-down or FRET to ask whether post-stimulus cells differ from naive cells in residence time, bound fraction, and dimer identity (e.g., long-lived FRA1-JUND replacing transient FOS-JUN) at matched total activity. This tests whether memory is stored in binding kinetics and partner choice rather than in AP-1 abundance.

ideas.title: Motif-matched surrogate bZIP swap
ideas.description: In an AP-1-null or degron-depleted background, re-express a chimera carrying the AP-1 bZIP DNA-binding domain fused to a minimal heterologous activation domain, so the same motifs are bound and activated by a protein lacking AP-1's native cofactor and pioneer interactions. If the surrogate restores acute induction but not persistence, memory resides in AP-1 protein surfaces rather than in motif occupancy per se.

ideas.title: Write AP-1 activity history into DNA with a molecular recorder
ideas.description: Drive a prime-editing or recombinase-based recorder (ENGRAM/DNA-Typewriter-style) from an AP-1-responsive promoter so each cell accumulates an ordered, cumulative record of its past AP-1 activity, then read the record and the current transcriptome from the same single cell. This decouples integrated past AP-1 dose from present state without sorting or fixing cells at an arbitrarily chosen early timepoint.
